thread.title: GDX: Buy And Hold Does Not Always Work - VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF (NYSEARCA:GDX)

author: Taylor Dart
title: GDX: Buy And Hold Does Not Always Work - VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF (NYSEARCA:GDX)
text:
The Tahoe Resources ( TAHO ) takeover earlier this month may have been exciting for traders, but it was a huge disappointment for most investors. While the stock was bought out for 60% above its 52-week lows, it was also bought out for 75% below its 2016 highs. Many mining analysts that have given ill-timed recommendations which are now down 60% or more continue to tell investors that the only way they can lose is by panicking and selling at a loss. While this may be true for blue chips like Apple ( AAPL ), Clorox ( JPM ), or JPMorgan ( JPM ) which will never be acquired for 25 cents on the dollar, it is not true for miners ( GDXJ ). During unfavorable periods for gold miners and metals ( GLD ), miners are often bought out for 60-80% off their highs. Tahoe Resources and Klondex Mines are a couple of recent examples of this. In this case, investors have no way to recoup their losses as the company ceases to exist.
(Source: TC2000.com)
While perusing the boards of different stock companies, it's alarming to see how many investors believe that holding and hoping is a strategy. Hope has no place in any investment strategy, and holding cyclical stocks over the long-run is not a sound strategy either. While growth companies or those that consistently pay dividends may be fine to buy and tuck away for a couple of decades, cyclical stocks are rarely ever "buy and forget" type investments. Cyclical stocks move in cycles by nature (hence their name), and holding these stocks long-term does not achieve anything except guarantee volatility in one's portfolio.
The prevailing wisdom from many mining analysts is that the only way to lose is by panic selling or impatiently selling, because according to them, eventually, these stocks will return to their cycle highs. I hate to be the one to burst this bubble, but it's not true in the slightest. Eldorado Gold ( EGO ) would need to rally 4000% to get back to its all-time highs, and many of these stocks will never see their cycle highs as larger companies are buying them out in the process. There is no way to merely wait for a stock to return to its 2016 highs to bail you out of your position if a stock is acquired as you are forced to tender your shares if the vote goes through to accept the deal. I will discuss a couple of recent examples of this below:
The "Take-Unders" Klondex Mines ( KLDX ) was bought out for just above $3.00 CAD, which happened to be more than 60% off of the stock's highs. If one had decided to take the Hecla ( HL ) shares and not sell them in hopes that they could recoup their money this way, their Hecla shares are now down an extra 32%. The premium on the Klondex deal is almost completely erased now.
(Source: TC2000.com)
Another recent take-under was Tahoe Resources which was bought out for nearly 90% from its all-time highs (after the premium), and 80% off of its 2016 highs by Pan American Silver ( PAAS ). It is impossible to ride Tahoe shares back up to $10.00 per share to get out at break-even or better if those shares are taken off the market. I fortunately observed this phenomenon in late 2011 and sold all of my junior miners despite being peddled the same promises that one day they would return to their highs. By the time 2015 came, most of them ceased to exist after being taken over for pennies. Had I not sold those stocks, I would have seen massive losses in my accounts.
(Source: TC2000.com)
For those who have been investing in juniors for the past decade, they might remember a stock called Canaco Resources that had all the mining analysts in a frenzy as it was the next major African gold discovery. The stock saw price targets of $7.00+ slapped on it but were eventually reduced to rubble when those chasing the stock higher sobered up during a weaker gold market. The stock was made famous by its discoveries at its Magambazi deposit in eastern Tanzania.
(Source: Financial Post)
Canaco Resources began to plummet after the floor came out from under the gold price and the projections for Magambazi were seen as far too optimistic.
(Source: StockCharts.com)
Canaco Resources eventually did a complicated reverse takeover where its assets where split up among different companies, after the stock fell 95% from its all-time highs. Those investors waiting for the 'cycle high' promised by many mining analysts have endured almost a decade long wait so far.
(Source: TC2000.com)
The worst case of wealth destruction was Allied Nevada Gold, a name that was touted by several mining analysts on stock boards that eventually went under. Some investors accumulating 100,000 shares or more of ElDorado seem to have forgotten about Allied Nevada Gold, a $2.6 billion Nevada gold producer. The stock was doing fine trading at over $40.00, and then was de-listed in a span of only two years. This is not to suggest this has to happen to Eldorado Gold, but much bigger companies have gone under before, and zero is always a possibility in this sector, even if that possibility is only 5% or so. Debt, questionable decisions by management and a gold price that made it difficult for them to make money on their projects ultimately was responsible for most of the stock's demise. This nightmare for Allied Nevada Gold shareholders did not occur at $800/oz or $400/oz gold, the company went under at gold prices over $1,200/oz.
The trouble for ElDorado Gold shareholders now is that even if it is bought out, it's now 97% from its all-time highs, and 90% from its 2016 highs. The stock has been a complete avoid all the way down as we can see from the trend band which has been running above it this whole time. In 99% of cases, I will never buy stocks that are below this trend band (red line) unless it is for extremely short-term trades with tight stops. Pan American Silver bought Tahoe Resources for a 35% premium to its 20-day VWAP (volume weighted average price). If Eldorado were to get the same generous premium based on its current 20-day VWAP of $0.63, it would be acquired for $0.85 a share. That is assuming someone decides to buy the company, assuming they get a generous premium and assuming the deal is done next week. While a hypothetical buy-out at $0.85 might help those who bought in the last month, it helps no one else.
I initially warned to avoid the stock at $3.60, and again recently at just below $1.00.
(Source: TC2000.com)
(Source: TC2000.com)
(Source: TC2000.com)
There has been no reason to buy a single share of Eldorado Gold, Sibanye Gold ( SBGL ), Tahoe Resources ( TAHO ) or many other miners over the past 18 months as they have all been locked in intermediate downtrends. While they may look cheap or oversold, momentum will ultimately dictate where they're going to go. Many gold companies just three years ago were trading for only 40-50% above cash levels in 2015 despite minimal debt. Valuations always swing past where they belong, and this is why I never try to sell the top, and I never try to buy the bottom. If there's one takeaway from this, it's that fundamentals are meaningless on the way down in cyclical companies. Analysts might be able to find 1000 reasons a stock should go up, but the fact that the price is not going up or bottoming is all one needs to know. If the fundamentals were indeed that good, the stock would be carving out a bottom by now as funds would be accumulating.
So what happens if we do buy on the way down? We are all human after all, and we all make mistakes. The key when making a mistake is to correct it immediately. I bought Alio Gold ( ALO ) at $4.25 in early 2017 because it looked like it had bottomed, but once it rallied to $5.00 the selling came in immediately. The heavy selling pressure after only a 20% rally told me there was big money that wanted out of their positions at any hint of an appreciation in share price. I cut my losses at 7% and got out of the stock immediately because it was not acting properly . The stock is now trading close to 70% lower. There is no need to have an ego, especially when dealing with speculative stocks. If a trade doesn't go as planned, pack your bags and move onto the next one. It's those traders that trade without any stops and are convinced they must be right that eventually stop trading as they have no money left.
If you make a mistake in trading, the best move is to fix it immediately. Compounding a single error by adding to a losing position is how an investor goes from having a small loss to completely hemorrhaging their portfolio. The market does not care where we're long from, and it doesn't care how much financial pain will be delivered to us if the price continues to drop. In cases where mining companies operate in risky jurisdictions with boards that make questionable decisions repeatedly, this risk is magnified. Management teams are allowed one or two strikes, but once you get to the point of three plus strikes, you are out. Funds want nothing to do with you, and it becomes a race to liquidate before other funds do. The reason for this is because funds know that they cannot reasonably sell their stakes when the only buyers that remain are retail investors. This is why we saw heavy liquidation of Eldorado Gold shares over the past several months; it was a race to the exits by funds. We can see proof of this in the funds holding Eldorado Gold has dropped from 600 in November 2016 down to 220 at the most recent quarterly filing.
The point of this article is to dispel the myth that buy and hold works in cyclical sectors with highly speculative stocks. While investors and traders may get away with poorly timed purchased in stocks like Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), or even Franco Nevada ( FNV ) as long as they don't use margin, the same is not true when dealing with most miners. The lower the market capitalization, the higher the debt, the worse the management team, and the higher the costs to produce gold all contribute to the risk of an investment in a gold miner. If a gold company can't reasonably pay down its debt and has weak margins, it's not going to have much success building out projects where it has better margins as it won't be able to borrow more to finance new project construction. Unfortunately, as we saw with Allied Nevada Gold, even those names that look relatively spotless can still surprise massively to the downside.
I continue to have no exposure to any miners ( GDXJ ) as none meet my criteria currently. I want to trade in bull markets or at the first signs of a new bull market, I have no interest in trying to catch bottoms. Those analysts who have been trying to catch the bottom in the miners over the past 18 months are learning a lesson that it's an exercise in futility. With no miners that meet my criteria for buying currently, I will remain patient. As a great trader once said:
"Remember this: When you are doing nothing, those speculators who feel they must trade day in and day out, are laying the foundation for your next venture. You will reap benefits from their mistakes."
